Any simple or variable WooCommerce product can be sold as appointments. The setup wizard creates or prepares one for you; for more products, or to fine-tune one, open the product and go to Product data → Slotiva.

Field What it does Bookable product Turns booking on for this product. The time picker appears at checkout when it is in the cart. Slot length (minutes) How long one appointment lasts. A multiple of 15, from 15 to 480 (8 hours). Minimum slots / Maximum slots How many times a customer can book in one order, from 1 to 10 (minimum ≤ maximum). For 2–3 hour sessions set the maximum to 3 and use Per slot pricing. Pricing Per slot — the product price is for one time; the cart quantity follows the number of times chosen. Fixed (single slot) — one price for one appointment. Location Optional. Shown with the appointment (for example an address or "Online"). Earliest booking (hours ahead) Optional. Leave empty to use the general rule on Slotiva → Working hours. Latest booking (days ahead) Optional, 1 to 62. Leave empty to use the general rule. Cancellation and change policy Optional. Leave empty to use the general policy from Slotiva → Settings. If a value is not valid (for example a length of 50 or 600 minutes), WooCommerce shows an error at the top of the product page — for the length: Slotiva: the slot length must be a multiple of 15 minutes (15 to 480). — and none of the Slotiva fields are saved, so the product keeps its previous settings.

The price is the product's normal WooCommerce price. With Per slot pricing it is the price of one time: a customer who books three times pays three times the price. A price of 0 is allowed (for example a free first consultation).
Slotiva → Settings → Bookable products lists every bookable product with its length, hours per order and pricing, and links to each product's Slotiva tab.

documents.t: Slotiva → Settings collects what is not tied to working hours.

Every bookable product with its length, hours per order and pricing (Fixed or Per slot). Open Slotiva tab goes to the product's own settings; + New bookable product and Open the setup wizard start the wizard. See Bookable product.

Cancellation and change policy — your text is shown to the customer under the time picker and with the appointment on the order page. Leave it empty to show nothing. A product can replace it with its own text.

Keep personal details for (default 24 months, 1 to 120) — after this, the name, email and phone of past appointments are anonymised. The appointment record (date, service, status) stays for statistics. Delete all Slotiva data when the plugin is deleted — off by default: deleting the plugin keeps appointments, working hours and settings. When on, deleting the plugin removes them for good. WooCommerce orders are never touched. WordPress's own personal data export and erasure tools (Tools → Export / Erase Personal Data) include appointments and their history.

Appointment emails are WooCommerce emails. Turn each one on or off and edit its subject and text in WooCommerce → Settings → Emails (the Open WooCommerce email settings button takes you there). Email Sent to When Booking confirmed Customer Once per order, when every appointment of the order is confirmed. Booking reminder Customer Before the appointment — set the time on Slotiva → Working hours (default 24 hours before). Booking time changed Customer You moved the appointment and ticked Email the new time to the customer. Booking cancelled Customer An appointment is cancelled, or a bank-transfer deadline passes. New booking Shop Once per order, when a booking is confirmed. Booking conflict Shop A paid order could not keep its time (see Appointments). Refund or set a new time by hand. These emails carry a calendar file (.ics); the cancellation email carries a calendar cancellation, so the appointment disappears from the customer's calendar app.
Everything on this page lives on Slotiva → Working hours. Changes take effect for new bookings as soon as you click Save changes; existing appointments are not moved.

Tick the days you work and set the hours. A day can have more than one range — click + range to add one. The gap between two ranges is a break (for example a lunch break: 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–18:00). Unticked days are closed. Customers can only pick times that fit completely inside a range.

Use Add closed or extra open time for one date: Closed — a holiday, a day off, or just a few hours. Extra open time — open on a day or at hours you normally do not work. Each entry can carry a short note for yourself. Entries are listed with a Delete link.

Rule Default What it does Appointment length 30 minutes Default length of one appointment. A product can set its own length on its Slotiva tab. A multiple of 15 minutes, at most 480 (8 hours). Earliest booking 24 hours ahead How soon a customer can book. With 24, a customer cannot book a time that starts in the next 24 hours. Latest booking 14 days ahead How far ahead customers can book (1 to 62 days). Break between appointments 0 minutes Free time kept after each appointment. Payment time for bank transfers 24 hours The time is held this long for a bank-transfer order. When it runs out, the order is cancelled and the time opens again. Hold time for card payments 45 minutes The time is held this long while a card payment completes (at least 15). If the payment does not arrive, the time opens again; the order itself is not cancelled. With PayTR, Slotiva automatically uses the longer of this value and PayTR's own time limit + 15 minutes; with other card providers, set it longer than the provider's time limit yourself. Reminder email On, 24 hours before Sends the customer a reminder before the appointment. Products can override Earliest booking and Latest booking on their own Slotiva tab — see Bookable product.

Slotiva shows and books every time in your site's time zone, set in Settings → General. Choose a city (for example Europe/Istanbul) rather than a fixed offset like UTC+3: a city follows daylight saving changes, a fixed offset does not. The setup wizard (step 4) warns you when a fixed offset is used. Slotiva releases expired holds by itself; you do not need to set up anything for that.

Slotiva → Appointments opens with four counters — Today, This week, Awaiting payment and Pay on site — and the list in four tabs: Today, Upcoming, Past and Cancelled. Each row shows the date and time, the customer and phone, the service, the appointment status, the payment status and the order. From the row you can Open the appointment, Change time or Cancel. All times are in your site's time zone (shown under the list).

Held — the customer is paying; the time is kept for them. Confirmed — booked. Completed / No-show — marked by you after the appointment. Cancelled. Expired — the payment did not arrive within the hold time; the time opened again. Conflict — a late payment arrived but the time was already taken (see below).

Click Open to see the customer, service, location, order, the number of changes used and the full History of the appointment. From here you can: Change time — pick a new day and time. The new time is locked first, then the old one is released, so nobody can take it in between. Tick Email the new time to the customer to send the Booking time changed email, and Count this as a change when the customer asked for it. Mark completed or Mark no-show after the appointment. Cancel appointment… — the time opens again (a Conflict appointment never held a time, so nothing opens). For a bank-transfer order that is awaiting payment, extend the payment window.

For phone or walk-in bookings, click + Add appointment, choose the service and a free time, and enter the customer's name (required), phone and email. The appointment is created without a WooCommerce order and marked Manual.
Export CSV downloads the list. The file opens correctly in Excel with Turkish settings (UTF-8, ; separator) and cells are made safe against spreadsheet formulas.

Sometimes a payment arrives after its hold has run out. If the time is still free, Slotiva books it again. If someone else has taken it meanwhile, the appointment is marked as a conflict and the shop receives the Booking conflict email: refund the order or set a new time by hand.
Slotiva adds no booking page of its own: your customer books on the WooCommerce checkout page, in the same step as paying.

When a bookable product is in the cart, the checkout shows Choose your times (or Choose your time when the product allows one time per order): a day strip with how many times are free on each day — closed days are marked; the free times of the selected day; Your selection, with the price and a button to remove each time. Customers can choose one or more times, also on different days, up to the product's maximum. With per-hour pricing the cart quantity follows the number of times chosen — the customer does not change the quantity themselves. If the customer presses Place order without choosing a time, the picker shows Choose a day and time for your booking., scrolls into view and takes the focus.

Two customers can look at the same free time. The first one to place the order gets it; the second sees that one of their times was just taken, the free times are refreshed and their details stay filled in, so they only choose again.

documents.t: Payment What happens to the time Card (for example PayTR) Held for the card payment window (Slotiva → Working hours, default 45 minutes). A failed payment keeps the hold, so the customer can retry from the order's payment page. Card orders are never cancelled automatically. Bank transfer Held until the transfer deadline (default 24 hours). If the money does not arrive, the order is cancelled and the time opens again. Pay on site, free orders Confirmed at once. A customer who already has several orders awaiting payment is asked to complete them before booking more.

The order confirmation page and My account → Orders show an appointment card for each booked time, with the date, time, time zone, service and its status (for example Awaiting payment, your time slot is being held). Confirmed appointments offer a calendar file (.ics) and a Google Calendar link. The customer also receives emails: booking confirmed, a reminder before the appointment, time changed and booking cancelled — see Settings and emails.

Check two things: The checkout page uses the Checkout block. The classic checkout ([woocommerce_checkout] shortcode) cannot sell bookable services; Slotiva shows a warning in WordPress admin when it is used. Open the checkout page in the editor, select the Classic Checkout block and choose Transform into blocks. The product in the cart is bookable: Bookable product is ticked on its Slotiva tab.
documents.s: The time picker does not appear at checkout

documents.t: The picker only offers times that are inside your working hours, not closed for that date, not already taken, and within the booking window: from Earliest booking (default 24 hours ahead) to Latest booking (default 14 days ahead). A long product length also needs a range long enough to fit it. Check Slotiva → Working hours and the product's Slotiva tab.
documents.s: A customer sees no free times

documents.t: Your site uses a fixed UTC offset (for example UTC+3) instead of a city. A fixed offset does not follow daylight saving changes. Choose your city in Settings → General → Timezone.
documents.s: The wizard says the time zone should be checked

documents.t: Customers cannot pay without one. Enable at least one payment method in WooCommerce → Settings → Payments. Bank transfer, card payments and pay on site all work with Slotiva.
documents.s: The wizard says no payment method is enabled

documents.t: Held means the customer has placed the order and is paying: nobody else can take the time, but the appointment is not booked yet. When the payment arrives it becomes Confirmed. If it does not arrive within the hold time, the time opens again. See What your customers see.
documents.s: What is the difference between "held" and "confirmed"?

documents.t: To stop one visitor from holding many times without paying, Slotiva limits how many unpaid bookings can wait at once. The customer should complete their earlier unpaid orders, or try again after those holds have run out.
documents.s: A customer says they cannot book: "too many bookings awaiting payment"

documents.t: Slotiva's emails are WooCommerce emails. Check that each one is enabled in WooCommerce → Settings → Emails and that your site can send email at all (WooCommerce's own order emails arrive). Many hosts need an SMTP plugin for reliable delivery.
documents.s: Customers do not receive the emails

documents.t: By default it is kept: appointments, working hours and settings stay in the database, and you find them again if you install Slotiva later. To remove everything when deleting the plugin, tick Delete all Slotiva data when the plugin is deleted on Slotiva → Settings first. WooCommerce orders are never deleted. Your license key is always removed when the plugin is deleted.
documents.s: What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

documents.t: No. Booking, payments, emails and all admin screens keep working. Only updates and support stop. See License and support.
documents.s: Does booking stop when my license ends?

documents.t: Minimum WordPress 7.0 PHP 8.1 WooCommerce 11.2 Database MySQL or MariaDB with InnoDB Checkout page Must use the WooCommerce Checkout block Slotiva is tested up to WordPress 7.1 and WooCommerce 11.3. The checkout page must use the Checkout block The time picker lives inside the WooCommerce Checkout block. The classic checkout (the [woocommerce_checkout] shortcode) cannot sell bookable services. If your checkout page is still classic, Slotiva shows a warning in WordPress admin, and the setup wizard offers a button that opens the page so you can convert it to blocks.

Slotiva is a paid plugin sold at wpalemi.com; it is not on WordPress.org. Download the ZIP file from your wpalemi.com account. In WordPress go to Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin, choose the ZIP and click Install Now. Click Activate.

Right after you activate it, Slotiva opens the setup wizard. It walks you through your service, your working hours, your bookable product and a check of your checkout page. Continue with the setup wizard. You can also choose Skip for now, I'll finish later. Until the setup is complete, a checklist on Slotiva → Appointments shows what is still missing, and you can open the wizard again at any time from Slotiva → Settings.
Booking, payments, emails and every admin screen work without a license. A license turns on updates and support. You can enter your key later on Slotiva → License — see License.

While your license is active, Slotiva tells you when a new version is out: on the Plugins screen under Slotiva, and at the top of Slotiva → License. To update: Download the new ZIP from your wpalemi.com account. Go to Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin and upload it. WordPress asks whether to replace the installed version with the uploaded one — choose Replace current with uploaded. Your appointments, working hours and settings are kept. Updating does not open the setup wizard again.

The wizard opens right after you activate Slotiva. It takes about three minutes and every answer can be changed later. You can leave at any time with Finish later; your progress is saved step by step.

Choose what you sell: Consulting, Lesson / training, Appointment / session or Another service. Slotiva uses your choice to suggest lengths and wording. Then choose how long one appointment lasts: 30, 45, 60, 90 or 120 minutes, or Other… for any multiple of 15 minutes from 15 to 480 (8 hours). The length you pick here is one "hour" your customer books. Customers who want longer sessions can book several in a row — you allow that in step 3.

Start from a ready-made pattern — Weekdays 9–18, Evenings 16–22, Mon–Sat, Every day 10–20 or Weekdays with a lunch break — then adjust the days. The panel on the right shows what your customers will see at checkout and how many appointments fit in a day and a week. At least one day must be open to continue: a store with no open hours has nothing to sell.

Decide what the customer buys: Create a new product — enter a name and the price of one hour. Slotiva creates a published, virtual WooCommerce product. Use an existing product — pick one of your products and set its price of one hour. If the product is a draft or private, the wizard tells you it will be published. The price must be a valid number; 0 is allowed (for example a free first consultation). Otherwise the wizard says Enter a valid price. If the product you pick is already bookable, it keeps its own length, minimum hours (never more than the maximum you choose) and pricing — running the wizard again does not reset them (only answering Yes below switches a fixed-price product to a price per hour). When its length differs from the one in step 1, the step says This product keeps its own length (… min). Change it in the product’s Slotiva tab., and the customer preview and the summary in step 5 use the product's length. Then answer Can a customer book more than one hour at a time? No, one hour — one appointment per order, fixed price. Yes — the price is multiplied by the number of hours. Set At most per order (2 to 10); the table below shows the price for each number of hours.

Slotiva checks three things every time this step opens: Time zone — a city time zone (for example Europe/Istanbul) is fine. A fixed UTC offset (such as +03:00) is marked Check, because it does not follow daylight saving changes. Change it in Settings → General. Payment method — at least one payment method should be enabled in WooCommerce. If none is, the row says Turn one on in WooCommerce → Settings → Payments. Checkout block — the checkout page must use the Checkout block. If it does not, the button Convert the checkout page to blocks opens the page editor: select the Classic Checkout block and choose Transform into blocks. Every row that needs attention has a How to fix link to the matching answer in the FAQ (opens in a new tab). Items marked Check do not stop you; you can continue or choose I'll do this later.

A summary of your service, working hours, product and checkout page. Change takes you back to that step (the checkout row has it only when something needs attention). Before your first customer, use Try a booking (opens your product page in a new tab) to book a test appointment yourself: see the time close and the emails arrive. At the bottom, First-time setup guide opens this page in a new tab.

Until the three required items — working hours, checkout page and a bookable product — are done, Slotiva → Appointments shows a checklist above the list. It disappears by itself once setup is complete, or you can hide it.

Go to Slotiva → Settings and click Open the setup wizard. It starts with your current settings and your existing bookable product selected. An existing bookable product keeps its own length, minimum hours and pricing (see step 3).

MHM Slotiva turns a WooCommerce product into a bookable service sold by the hour: a consultation, a private lesson, a therapy session, a coaching call. Your customer chooses a day and one or more times inside the WooCommerce checkout page and pays for the order in one step. While the payment is pending, the time is held for them, so two customers can never book the same time.

The customer adds your service to the cart and goes to the checkout. On the checkout page they pick a day and one or more times. Times can be on different days. With per-hour pricing the cart quantity follows the number of times they choose. They place the order. Slotiva holds the chosen times while the payment is completed: Card payment: the time is held for the card payment window (45 minutes by default). Bank transfer: the time is held until the transfer deadline (24 hours by default). If no payment arrives, the order is cancelled and the time opens again. Pay on site and free orders: the appointment is confirmed at once. The appointment is confirmed and the customer gets an email with a calendar file. They also see their appointments on the order page and in My account. You manage it in WordPress: Slotiva → Appointments shows today's, upcoming, past and cancelled appointments. You can change the time, cancel, or add appointments by hand.
Anyone who sells time: consultants, tutors and teachers, clinics and therapists, coaches. One store can have several bookable products, each with its own length, price and number of hours per order.
Choosing a staff member (doctor, teacher) for the appointment. Capacity: more than one customer in the same time (group classes).
Install Slotiva and check the requirements. Run the setup wizard — it takes a few minutes.

Booking works without a license. All admin screens stay open; a license only unlocks: Updates — when a new version is out, the Plugins page tells you and you download it from your account. Support — answers to setup and usage questions by email. New features — every version released during your license is included.

Open Slotiva → License, paste your key and click Activate license. The key is in your purchase email and in your account. It is stored on your site and never shown again in full — the screen shows only its first 4 characters.
The license screen always shows one of these states. Once a key is entered, About this license status at the bottom of the screen opens the matching section of this page in a new tab.
Updates and support are on. The screen shows the days left, the end date, when the license was last checked (Check now checks again) and a link to your account.

The license ends within 14 days. Updates and support still work; renew and they continue without a break — if your subscription renews automatically, there is nothing to do. Manage subscription opens your account; How does renewal work? opens the Expired section of this page; Check now checks the license again, for example right after you renewed.

The end date has passed. What keeps working: booking, payments, emails and every admin screen. What stops: new-version notices, the right to download new versions, and support. Renew license opens your account; renewing brings updates and support back at once. If you have a different key, enter it under Have a different key?.

The key was accepted but could not be verified on this site. Updates are paused; booking is not affected. Click Check now. If you recently changed the site address, deactivate the license on this site and activate it again. If it continues, contact support.

Slotiva could not reach the license server. Updates stay on for up to 7 days after the last successful check; if the connection comes back in that time, nothing changes. The grace period never goes past the license end date. Check now tries again.

While updates are on, a strip at the top of the license screen announces a new version (Slotiva … is out.). Click Download … to get the ZIP from your account, then install it via Plugins → Add Plugin → Upload Plugin — see Installation.

documents.t: A license works on one site. Click Deactivate on this site (shown in every state) to release it; you can then activate the key on another site. Booking keeps working on the old one.
documents.s: Moving the license to another site

documents.t: Support questions go through your account at wpalemi.com. Please include your Slotiva version (shown on the Plugins screen) and what you were doing when the problem appeared.
